articles.title: Racist text sent to Dearica Hamby results in employee's firing
articles.summary: Hamby exposed the message last month.
articles.body:
A racist text message screenshot and shared by Los Angeles Sparks star Dearica Hamby has resulted in the sender's dismissal from their position at the medical equipment supplier Acclaro Medical.

On Aug. 24, Hamby revealed on social media a text sent to her personal phone number. She asked her 47,000 followers on X for help in identifying the sender, who included their own personal phone number with Florida area code 561.

Acclaro Medical was quickly alerted to the text after internet sleuths tracked down the sender's phone number. The employee was suspended shortly thereafter, and Acclaro Medical confirmed to USA Today on Tuesday that the person had been fired.

Hamby, a three-time All-Star and two-time Sixth Player of the Year winner, is the latest WNBA player to receive racist messages or threats as the league continues to grapple with external challenges.

Las Vegas Aces guard Chelsea Gray exposed racist direct messages she received in July, which similarly led to the sender's dismissal from their job .

After Alyssa Thomas garnered a one-game suspension for a fist to Caitlin Clark's throat in June, the Phoenix Mercury star revealed that she had received death threats in addition to racist messages online. Thomas directly called out beleaguered WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert and implored her to do more to protect the league from threats of this nature.

articles.title: LaMelo Ball says Jaylen Brown better than Boston Celtics Jayson Tatum, maybe Larry Bird
articles.summary: "I have got to see all the accolades," said Ball, "but if you line up Boston's best players ever, he's in my top five."
articles.body:
Few among us know NBA basketball like the players who make up that league. And while that may not come as much of a surprise to most fans of the sport, the fact that recency bias can warp the perception of historical greatness ought to not come as much of a shock either given not all of us (NBA stars or otherwise) are scholars of league history.

So when new Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball paid former Boston Celtics forward Jaylen Brown near the top of the mountain when it comes to all-time great Celtics on a recent episode of the semi-eponymous "Ball in the Family" podcast, one can hardly blame him, especially considering he was not all that far from the truth. "I have got to see all the accolades," said Ball ( h/t to Yahoo Sports' Gautam Varier) with an understandable caveat, "but if you line up Boston's best players ever, he's in my top five."

Now if you were to say top at his position, that would be a more reasonable argument given the existence of players like Bill Russell, Bob Cousy, John Havlicek, Jo Jo White, Dave Cowens, Robert Parish, Kevin McHale, Larry Bird, Paul Pierce, and Kevin Garnett. There are reasonable arguments to rank him three or maybe even four of those names, but after that it gets tough given all these Hall of Fame players accomplished in Boston. Ball seemed to acknowledge this dynamic, shifting the frame to a more positional one.

"Only two wings is better than him is Paul Pierce and Larry Bird," said the Minnesota guard. Hondo and White would like a word, but to be fair neither looms as large in the lore of the wider league as they ought to. Perhaps most interestingly, Ball also thinks Boston dealt their best player to the Philadelphia 76ers.

"I think Brown's a little better," said Ball. "He's low-key frying Bird ... I don't want to be disrespectful… Bird is baking him too, but he's baking Bird. Bird is baking him, too, but he is also getting to it ... Jaylen Brown has a better chance of guarding him than he has of guarding Jaylen Brown."

Forgive us if we're quite skeptical of the latter take. But for at least last season (and arguably until proven otherwise), Ball has a leg to stand on in the Jayson Tatum-Brown debate. But so long as the St. Louis native has two healthy legs to stand on, we're of the opinion that debate will soon be quashed in Tatum's favor as well – as good as Brown may be.

articles.title: Kate Martin signs developmental contract with Sky days after Sparks exit
articles.summary: Kate Martin has a new home. She's heading to the Chicago Sky, not far from where she grew up in Edwardsville, Illinois.
articles.body:
Kate Martin's professional basketball journey continues in the Windy City.

On Wednesday, the Chicago Sky announced they signed Edwardsville, Illinois, native to a developmental contract. The news comes less than a week after the Los Angeles Sparks waived the 6-foot guard on Aug. 29.

Martin, drafted with the 18th overall pick by the Las Vegas Aces in the 2024 WNBA Draft, was one of four second-round selections to make a WNBA roster that same year. The ouster from the Sparks marked her second time being cut this season.

The 26-year-old was waived by the Golden State Valkyries on May 7, after spending the 2025 campaign with the team, averaging 6.2 points and 2.7 rebounds in 16.4 minutes per game. She was originally picked up in the 2024 expansion draft by the franchise. On May 10, the Sparks signed Martin to a developmental roster spot. Developmental players are eligible to play in 12 regular-season games before they must be converted to a standard contract.

"My role right now is to be the best developmental player I can possibly be. Get in extra workouts. Be a great teammate. Do whatever the team needs me to do. Be a great hype woman on the bench," Martin said in May.

"We're still learning kind of what the development role kind of entails, but as of now, it's to be where my feet are, buy in to being an L.A. Spark, and give it all I got."

2026 WNBA season is underway. See photos from the league's 30th year

On July 6, the Sparks made Martin the first player in franchise history to be upgraded from the development pool to a standard WNBA contract, with now-fired general manager Raegan Pebley lauding Martin's "versatility on both ends of the floor." However, that same month, Martin's usage decreased significantly.

Even after Sparks coach Lynne Roberts said in August that the team's ownership had "asked that bench players receive playing time rest of the season" with the Sparks having clinched a losing record and missing the playoffs, Martin's play was limited. Roberts attributed the situation to the front office already having data on Martin while other players needed the time to prove themselves. The guard finished her time in Los Angeles playing 17 games with the Sparks, averaging 2.3 points per game.

Before her WNBA career, Martin played seasons at Iowa, where she averaged 8.0 points on 46.4% from the field, 4.6 rebounds and 2.9 assists. She appeared in 163 career games for Iowa and ranks fifth in Hawkeyes history in assists (473).

Martin is expected to be available for Chicago when the WNBA returns from the FIBA World Cup break on Sept. 17. If Martin plays, her Sky debut would be against the Washington Mystics (8 p.m. ET, League Pass).

Dallas Wings center Li Yueru won't be representing China in the FIBA Women's World Cup due to passport issues.

Li announced on social media her passport "was lost in the mail and still hasn't been found" (via the Associated Press' Doug Feinberg ).

"Throughout this time, we've all been working hard together and exploring every possible solution, but maybe we were just a little short on luck this time," she said. "As of today, the passport is still missing.
